newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Dollar spurts, shares fall on Lebed sacking.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Dollar spurts, shares fall on Lebed sacking.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin's decision to fire his security chief, Alexander Lebed, jolted the dollar higher against the mark on Thursday and prompted European stock markets to retreat.
The dollar leapt half a pfennig as concerns about political instability in Moscow pressured the German currency and Swiss franc.
Share markets in both Germany and France also pared gains after the news from Moscow.

Following an increasingly rancorous struggle in the Kremlin between Interior Minister Anatoly Kulikov and Lebed, Yeltsin appeared on television to announce he had sacked his security chief who had been accused of plotting to seize power.
"This is disturbing news for European assets given the potential for increased political instability in Russia," said Keith Edmonds, chief analyst at IBJ International in London.
Russian financial markets had already spent a jumpy day that saw sharp falls in shares and bonds.
"There was panic in the morning," said a trader at the Troika-Dialog bank in Moscow. "The market is very sensitive to political news and it causes panicky movements from both brokers and investors."
Share traders in France and Germany blamed the Lebed news for a turndown in share prices, but London dealers were focused more on a string of U.S. figures.
British shares originally stayed firm after U.S. jobless claims and housing starts came in largely as expected.

But tame U.S. economic data did nothing to quash concerns about U.S. corporate earnings data and London slipped with Wall Street. By 1445 GMT the Dow was trading nearly 11 points up 6,032 but well off its highs for the day.
Some foreign exchange analysts said they thought the impact of the Lebed sacking on the dollar would be limited.
"The sentiment for the dollar is really very positive anyway right now," said Gabriele Lamers, an international economist at Bank of Boston.
"(Lebed's dismissal) is just one of those other things that is helping the dollar at the moment."
By 1445 the dollar was trading at 1.5435 marks and 112.13 yen, compared with 1.5383 and 112.22 in late European business on Wednesday.
French shares, which had earlier reacted positively to the U.S. data, pared their gains by late afternoon, with the CAC-40 index back to opening levels.
A one-day strike by public sector workers appeared to have little effect on markets.
German shares also pared gains in after hours computerised trading as equities tracked government bonds lower on the Lebed sacking.
German markets often react strongly to events in Russia because of the country's involvement in the Russian economy.
CURRENCIES AT 1445 GMT
The dollar was trading at 1.5435 marks and 112.13 yen, compared with 1.5383 and 112.22 in late European business on Wednesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1445 GMT
London - The FTSE index was up 11.9 points at 4,036.3.
Frankfurt - The 30-share DAX index closed up 0.13 points at 2,716.26. In later screen-based trade the IBIS DAX was up 8.63 at 2,713.69.
Paris - The CAC-40 share index was up 0.13 points at 2,158.65.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold fixed at $380.60 against $380.55 in the morning after testing support at $380. Silver also slipped 12 cents to $4.94.
